author: Sharjeel Hashmat
title: Myth: rising transaction value means rising prices
description: Dubai transaction value rose 31% in Q1 2026 while the number of transactions rose 6%. Value is a total, not a price, and the two can move apart.

body.p: A headline reports record transaction value and readers hear "prices are up". Value is the total of everything sold. It moves with how many deals happen and how large each one is, as well as with price.
The Dubai Land Department reported Q1 2026 real estate transactions worth AED 252 billion, up 31% year on year, while the number of real estate transactions rose 6% to 60,303.
Value grew about five times as fast as the count. That gap can come from higher prices, from larger or more expensive properties changing hands, or from both. The release does not separate them.

Value is deals multiplied by deal size. It can rise while the price per square foot is flat if more expensive units trade, and it can fall while prices hold if fewer deals happen. A headline about value cannot tell you which of those happened.

ul: Ask which measure a headline uses: value, volume or price per square foot.
Compare price per square foot in your building and unit type. A citywide figure cannot tell you what your unit is worth.
Treat one quarter as one data point.

body.p: The Dubai Land Department publishes a residential price index, but its own page says the index should not be used for pricing and investment decision making. That is a reason to check transactions in your own building.

sources.name: Dubai Land Department: Dubai real estate transactions reach AED 252 billion in Q1 2026
Dubai Land Department: Dubai Residential House Price Index (DRHPI) disclaimer
Dubai Media Office: Dubai real estate transactions surge 31% to reach AED252 billion in Q1 2026

draftNotes: Every figure is from the DLD Q1 release and the Dubai Media Office copy of it, both re-read on 2026-09-21: AED 252 billion, +31%, 60,303 transactions, +6%, released 9 April 2026.

"About five times as fast" is 31% divided by 6%. The release does not define "transactions" beyond "real estate transactions" and lists 718,160 "procedures" separately, so I did not compute an average deal size.

The quote about the price index is from the DLD page's own disclaimer: "should not be used for any commercial purposes, including pricing and investment decision making or performance measurement." The page calls its index the DRHPI.
